title: Flu Cases High as Early Outbreak Spreads in Japan
paragraphs: Japan is facing an unusually early and large flu outbreak this year, with the number of cases rising sharply in the autumn.

On August 28, Japan's health ministry announced that the country's flu season had officially begun. In the week before the announcement, an average of 1.11 flu patients were reported at each of the roughly 3,000 medical institutions that report flu cases to the government. A figure of 1 or higher is considered the start of the flu season. This was the second-earliest start since 1999, when the current system for tracking infectious diseases began. The earliest start was in 2009.
At the beginning of the season, the southern prefecture of Okinawa had the most cases, with 4.43 patients per institution. Iwate and Aomori, in the north of Japan, also had relatively high numbers.

Since then, the outbreak has grown rapidly. According to China's Xinhua news agency, 42,320 flu cases were reported across Japan in the week from September 28 to October 4. That was about 7.3 times the number reported in the same period last year. The average number of patients per medical institution reached 11.35, the first time this season that the figure had reached the "caution" level.
The outbreak has also spread in Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan, an area that was recently hit by a powerful earthquake.
An early flu season can put serious pressure on hospitals and schools. Older people and young children are especially at risk of serious illness from the flu.

The health ministry has urged people to protect themselves by washing their hands regularly, wearing masks and getting vaccinated. Japan also experienced an early flu outbreak last year, when the government declared a nationwide epidemic in October. Some experts have been discussing whether these early outbreaks are a sign that the pattern of the flu season is changing.
